title: Shorten verify.rs judge below 200 lines by extracting helpers
summary: Refactor `judge` in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs (205 lines, limit 200) by moving the "commands seen running" computation into a private helper, with no behavior change. The goal is for code health to pass; the audience is the verifier and code health.

defaults_applied.how: BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions:
Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs: judge (lines 408-675) builds `ran` and `revert_runs` (lines 411-445, no format! strings), then findings; test `drift_haystack` (line ~3251) slices source from `
pub fn judge(` to the first `
}
` and scans its format! literals, so strings carrying rule sources must stay in judge. No record files are added.
Extracting the ~35-line `ran`/`revert_runs` computation saves enough lines to get under 200; a file split is unnecessary since the file is 577 production lines.
The helper must not be placed so that the first `\n}\n` after `pub fn judge(` changes; the helper goes before judge.

acceptance_criteria.text: In crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs, `pub fn judge` spans at most 200 lines (Grep `pub fn judge(` and read to its closing brace in the diff/snapshot); no other production function exceeds 200 lines and the file stays under 2000 production lines.

The extracted logic (building `ran` from commands_run and passing checks, and `revert_runs`) lives in a private helper in verify.rs, and its body is moved unchanged (diff shows only relocation and parameter plumbing).

The `format!` strings that the drift test reads (including `must cite commands that ran (D43)`) remain inside the body of `judge`, so `drift_haystack` in the test module still finds them; the tests module is unchanged.
No behavior change: `cargo test -p athena-core` passes, including verify::tests and rule_sources_appear_in_the_header_or_judge_format_strings.
`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` report no issues, and `cargo test` passes.

departures: Small mechanical extraction with a known pitfall (drift test) identified, so slightly higher pass chance than the reference.
hard_reason: Touches judge, the function that computes the final verdict gating other jobs, so a mistake is costly and hard to see.
